meta: Need AI to summarize internal files, but your company forbids sending documents outside? Run an open model right on your computer: it works offline and your data never leaves.

muc.title: Files that can't leave
muc.text: Mark needs AI to summarize internal files, but his company forbids sending documents to outside services.

muc.title: A model on your own machine
muc.text: Bit suggests: run an open model right on your computer. Everything is processed locally, it works with the internet off, and your data never leaves the machine.

muc.title: Install it like an app
muc.text: There are now apps like Ollama or LM Studio that install like normal software: pick a model, download it, and chat.

muc.title: What your computer needs
muc.text: A laptop with 16 GB of RAM runs a model of about 8 billion parameters, quantized to 4 bits, quite well. A good GPU makes it faster.

muc.title: The trade-off
muc.text: In return, a small local model is weaker than the biggest cloud models, and slower. It's good for simple jobs like summarizing, translating and drafting.

muc.title: Try a small model
muc.text: If your computer has 16 GB of RAM or more, install an app that runs models, download a small model, turn off the internet and ask it a question.
